clips.send: A struggling business owner sends this to a friend pushing a dead product: the shame of selling something nobody wants, and the relief of hearing why.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says a man once offered him $50,000 just for a consultation on how to sell a product nobody wanted. Kevin turned him down and told him the truth: "Don't waste your money. That isn't going to sell."

His reason: "Why are you trying to make a pig sing? You waste your time and you annoy the pig." The product was never the problem. The need was missing.

clips.send: A discouraged founder sends this to a friend mid-failure: anger turned into resolve - proof Rockefeller and Edison counted failures as fuel, not a verdict to quit.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says John D. Rockefeller, worth an estimated $700 billion in today's money, put it simply: "In every adversity are the seeds of a greater benefit. You have to find them."

Thomas Edison failed to build the light bulb 10,000 times. Asked how that felt, his answer was: "I didn't fail 10,000 times. I successfully found 10,000 ways it didn't work."

That is the millionaire mindset Kevin Trudeau teaches: every failure is information, not a verdict. Comment "BRAIN" and I will send you the free training on how to think like this on purpose.
